the role of LMP1 in NPC and how it contributes to the metastatic potential of this tumor.
the role of LMP1 and its interaction with plakoglobin and beta-catenin in NPC metastasis.

the effects of the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) latent membrane protein-2 (LMP2) on cell migration, and the role of the EBV oncoproteins LMP1 and LMP2 in the pathogenesis of nasopharyngeals carcinoma (NPC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LMP1 induces the expression and stabilization of beta-catenin and a cadherin change, but not plakoglobin.
LMP1 decreases the amount of nuclear plakogobin, which in turn decreases the transcription of plakoglobin and leads to the loss of junctional plackoglobin.
the loss of plako-globin is not a major factor in the induction of migration by LMP1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EBV LMP1 promotes NPC cell migration through effects on the cadherin switch and the resultant effects on junctional proteins.
LMP1 induces a cadherin shift from E- to cadherin, which is a hallmark of cancer, and this shift is accompanied by a decrease in junctional plakoglobins.

LMP1 induces the cadherin switch by decreasing plakoglobin levels, but that the remaining junctional pool of plakoglobin can associate with the N-cadherins to restore junctional integrity and reduce migration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LMP1 induces and stabilizes beta-catenin while decreasing plakoglobin.

LMP1 can affect plakoglobin in a manner that contributes to the progression of NPC, and that the effects of plakoglobin on NPC progression can be distinguished by whether the cells express N-cadherins.
EBV LMP1 expression in nasopharygeal carcinoma cells decreases the levels of plakoglobulin in both the nucleus and junctional complexes, which may promote metastasis.
